turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas. The main formula for qualifying withdrawals on or after January 1, 2002 is **2.40% of final average salary for each year of service**, with a maximum annuity of **80% of final average salary**. Final average salary is generally the highest average annual salary for any **4 consecutive years within the last 10 years** of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

If you begin the annuity before age 60, the formula generally carries a reduction of **0.25% for each full month or fractional part of a month** that your age at the annuity’s start is below 60. Section 11-134 also lists exceptions for certain combinations of age and service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

Your **21.5 years of service** must be determined under the service-credit rules. For minimum-annuity purposes, Section 11-216 provides special service-counting rules, including that service during **6 or more months** in a year counts as a year of service and service of less than 6 months but at least 1 month counts as a half year. Section 11-215 also lists periods that may count as service, such as qualifying paid leave and certain disability periods. [40 ILCS 5/11-215] [40 ILCS 5/11-216]

The section does not by itself provide your pension amount. That would turn on your final-average-salary figure, your annuity starting date, and which of Section 11-134’s available formulas applies. I also could not establish any conclusion that depends on Sections 11-221 or 11-164, because those provisions were not before me.

I'm going by your record, which places you in Article 11 — tell me if that's not right.

Under Article 5, Section 5-132, a qualifying police officer with 25 years of service may receive an annuity based on the average salary for the four highest consecutive years in the last 10 years, subject to the section’s eligibility rules and limits. Section 5-238 is a separate Tier 2 provision and applies only to a person who first became a policeman on or after January 1, 2011. [40 ILCS 5/5-132] [40 ILCS 5/5-238]
